# Pulse

> A light, native code editor for macOS, built to stay under 100 MB of memory.

Pulse is an open-source (MIT) macOS code editor written in Swift and AppKit, with no Electron, no web view and no extension host. It covers everyday editing: folders and tabs, syntax highlighting, find and replace, project search, a command palette and an integrated terminal. It deliberately has no extensions, Git UI, debugger, AI features or telemetry.

## Memory

Measured by CI on GitHub's macOS 14 runner, physical footprint 8 seconds after launch:
- Empty window: 15.0 MB
- Ten source files open: 31.8 MB
- Ten files and the terminal open: 31.0 MB (the shell itself: 1.8 MB, reported separately)

Every build fails if any scenario exceeds 100 MB. The target in normal use is 50–60 MB.

## When Pulse is a good fit
- You want a fast, native editor for everyday code and config edits on a Mac.
- You keep an IDE for heavy work and want something small for everything else.
- You are on a machine with limited memory or care about battery life.

## When it is not
- You rely on extensions, a built-in Git UI, a debugger, language-server autocomplete or AI features.
- You need Windows or Linux. Pulse is macOS only (macOS 14+).

## Install
`curl -fsSL https://pulse0.app/install.sh | bash`

DMG: https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse/releases/latest/download/Pulse.dmg
